text: Unittest is Python's built-in framework for writing automated tests that check your code stays correct.
You group related tests inside a class that inherits from TestCase.
Each test is a method whose name starts with test, so the framework can find and run it.
[chuckle] assertEqual checks that two values match — here, that adding two and three really gives five.
[sniff] You write one test method per behavior you want to verify, keeping each focused and clear.
TestCase gives you many assertions — assertEqual, assertTrue, assertRaises, and assertIsInstance among them.
This last one confirms the result is actually an integer, not just the right number.
[sigh] Running the tests reports which passed and which failed, so a broken change gets caught immediately.
[groan] Automated tests are your safety net — they let you refactor fearlessly, knowing you'll catch anything you break.
